_what: The prose countdown for #492. One key per test file, the number of PROSE assertions it still carries, and nothing else. A prose assertion is one whose EXPECTED value is a fragment of a sentence the product composed - the class that stays green when the thing it names is broken. TestProseGuardTests derives the real figure from a Roslyn parse of the test sources every run and holds the two against each other. #492 is not complete while this file's total is above zero.
_how: Per file rather than one total so a reshaping PR deletes or lowers its own key instead of editing a number every other PR also edits: two reshapes of different files then merge cleanly. A file with no key allows ZERO, which is what stops a new file - the six probe conversions, #494 - from being written in the old shape. BOTH DIRECTIONS GATE: a file above its number fails as growth, and a file below it fails too, with 'delete the headroom', because a baseline left above the real figure stops being a countdown.
_the_rule: Derived, never listed. The eight xUnit string-assertion forms are found by syntax; argument 0 is the expected value and argument 1 the subject; the collection/predicate forms are outside the rule. A site is PROSE unless it is a catalogue-identity check (ReadSentences./WriteSentences.), structural (no literal at all, a collection, every literal a declared WIRE TOKEN, or a subject that is a document accessor not read back with .GetString()), or fixture-known (whitespace-free literals that a fixture file declares, or an expression naming a fixture symbol). The wire vocabulary, the fixture values and the fixture symbols are all derived from the source tree - see TestProseGuardTests for each rule.
_lowered_by: A reshaping PR: it asserts the engine fact on the json document keyed by the record (Facts.cs), or moves the sentence into ReadSentences byte-identically and asserts its identity (Facts.States), then lowers or deletes its key in the same commit. Nothing else in this file moves.
_raised_once: Raising a number is legal, deliberate and meant to be visible: the raise and the reason land in the same commit, argued once. That is what keeps this a countdown rather than headroom.
